llm.summary: This VMware audit and policy skill is mostly coherent, but its policy enforcement can be globally bypassed or fail open in ways users should review carefully before relying on it for production controls.

dimensions.detail: The skill stores persistent local audit data under ~/.vmware and exports audit logs; this matches the purpose, but exported logs and audit metadata may expose operational details and the documentation gives limited handling warnings.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv to install the vmware-policy package and allows Bash for CLI workflows; this is disclosed and coherent for a CLI/library skill, but it depends on external package contents not present in this artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Auto-loading for any VMware skill tool is broad, but it is consistent with the documented role as a shared decorator and audit/policy dependency across the VMware skill family.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent audit logging, hot-reloaded rules, and local configuration are expected, but the enforcement posture is under-scoped because missing rules, missing PyYAML, or a simple environment variable can allow all operations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is centralized audit logging, policy enforcement, and sanitization for 156+ VMware tools, but the artifacts document an unrestricted VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass and fail-open behavior when rules or PyYAML are missing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before using it as a production control. It appears intended to be a local audit/policy helper and does not advertise network exfiltration, but do not rely on enforcement unless you create ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, verify PyYAML is installed, protect ~/.vmware/audit.db, and avoid setting VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED except under tightly controlled emergency procedures.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the CLI reference documents VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 as a global policy bypass. A bypass may be useful for break-glass operations, but the artifact does not scope it to privileged, time-limited, or emergency use.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: activation on VMware tool calls is broad, but it matches the skill's stated role as infrastructure used by the VMware skill family rather than an unrelated trigger.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: capabilities.md states that VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypasses all policy checks while still logging ok_bypassed, which weakens the stated enforcement role.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly confirmed: exporting audit logs is expected for compliance workflows, but the artifact does not clearly warn that exported logs may contain sensitive operational metadata.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: setup-guide.md says operations are allowed when ~/.vmware/rules.yaml is absent, which is a fail-open default for a policy component unless the user intentionally wants audit-only mode.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: setup-guide.md documents VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED as a simple bypass without strong production-use warnings or compensating controls.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Confirmed: setup-guide.md says missing PyYAML causes PolicyEngine to silently allow all operations, which can leave users believing policy enforcement is active when it is not.
